provenance.paper_title: MemSlides: A Hierarchical Memory Driven Agent Framework for Personalized Slide Generation with Multi-turn Local Revision

representation_paths.memory_component: persistent user profile plus evolving session and slide-edit working state

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.1 Stateful Multi-turn Slide Authoring; Sec. 3.2 Plan-Act-Guard
evidence.paraphrase: The framework maintains a persistent user profile containing visual-style, layout, and template preferences together with an evolving session state. Working memory records temporary preferences, carryover constraints, edit targets, coverage, and snapshot hashes; the planner and actor read this state and the guard updates it after each local slide revision.

Profile memory persists across jobs while active working memory changes over revision rounds through append and supersede operations. At job completion, stable signals are consolidated into the long-term profile for use in later slide-generation jobs.

representation_paths.memory_component: compact lessons, tool-error summaries, and reusable operation-context fragments

evidence.paraphrase: Raw reasoning, tool-call, and observation chains are segmented into compact reusable fragments indexed by operation context. Relevant fragments are retrieved before similar future tool calls, while transferable round-level lessons and error patterns are consolidated into long-term experience memory.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.2 Plan-Act-Guard; Sec. 3.3 Hierarchical Memory
evidence.paraphrase: After each user feedback round, fixed append and supersede rules update the active preference, carryover, target, coverage, and snapshot state that will govern the next local revision.
The system transforms raw reasoning-tool-observation traces and round outcomes into reusable fragments, lessons, tool-error summaries, and operation patterns for later retrieval.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.3 Hierarchical Memory; Sec. 3.4 Experience Memory
evidence.paraphrase: At job completion, stable preference signals and transferable tool experience are consolidated from active working memory into persistent profile and long-term experience tiers for future slide-generation jobs.

derived.hybrid_relation: Structured profile and slide-edit state is joined with compact tool-experience records: Plan-Act-Guard reads both paths when planning and executing personalized slide generation and local visual revisions.

adjudication_notes: Included because memory directly controls non-text slide properties and operations: visual theme, layout, templates, local slide targets, and edits to the actual deck are persisted and reused, rather than memory serving only as textual background context.

Tier T2 applies because working, profile, and experience memory content changes across revision rounds and jobs under fixed procedures. The paper does not show deployment-time feedback modifying those management procedures, so T3 does not apply.
Full text was reviewed through the arXiv HTML rendering; it has stable section, figure, and equation anchors but no stable PDF page references were used.
